comparison: Both evaluate claims C45-C46 about fiber reorientation geometry. OpenEval finds the geometric reasoning sound and supported by Figure 6, while peer reviewers express uncertainty about fiber orientation assumptions, questioning whether alpha is an input parameter or consequence of deformation and requesting clarification on how alpha is chosen.

Both address energy conversion mechanism (C49-C51). OpenEval finds the mechanism theoretically sound within the model framework and supported by Appendix 5 Figure 1. Peer reviewers acknowledge it is 'convincing on the phenomenological level' but rate it UNCERTAIN, calling it 'very obscure' and requesting more microscopic-level details on how bending energy converts to elongation.

Both evaluate model validation against experimental data (C60). Both find the evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes good qualitative agreement in Figure 8B for wild-type and mutants. Peer reviewers confirm the model 'can be successfully fitted to the elongation dynamics' and is 'convincing on the phenomenological level.'

Both evaluate quantitative parameters C52-C55 about contraction timing and duration. Both find these claims SUPPORTED. OpenEval verifies the arithmetic is correct and parameters properly cited. Peer reviewers accept these empirical constraints from cited experimental data without challenge.

Both evaluate dissipation estimate C70 as UNCERTAIN. OpenEval notes the authors acknowledge significant limitations in calculation accuracy at late stages. Peer reviewers raise broader concerns about the energy transfer modeling being 'very obscure,' affecting confidence in quantitative energy predictions.

Both address potential applications C73-C74. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting these are explicitly speculative future directions without validation. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, with Reviewer 3 viewing the broader applicability to other organisms and soft robots as a strength of the framework.

Both evaluate experimental observations including C1 and C24 about embryo behavior. Both find these claims SUPPORTED as established background from cited literature. OpenEval notes these establish phenomena the model aims to explain; peer reviewers focus critiques on the model's explanation rather than questioning the phenomena themselves.

Both evaluate C20 about prior modeling work (Ben Amar et al., 2018). Both find this claim SUPPORTED as established background. OpenEval notes the prior model's limitation to 70% elongation motivates current work; peer reviewers accept this as unchallenged background for the study's focus on late elongation.

Both evaluate claims about two-stage elongation process (C16-C18) and related background. Both find these claims SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes appropriate citations and reference to Figure 1A as established experimental knowledge. Peer reviewers accept these as biological foundation for modeling work without challenge.

Both evaluate C. elegans model system characteristics (C11, C14, C15). Both find these claims SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes well-established characteristics with appropriate citations justifying model system choice. Peer reviewers accept these as rationale for studying this system without questioning the claims.

Both evaluate muscle importance and anatomy claims (C21-C22, with peer also covering C16-C18). Both find these claims SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes established experimental observations with citations and Figure 1B. Peer reviewers accept these as part of the biological foundation for modeling work.
